newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia company directors optimistic on economy.
newsitem.headline: Australia company directors optimistic on economy.

text.p: Directors from the construction/utilities and retail/wholesale sectors have become more optimistic about their companies' prospects during the past quarter, a survey released on Tuesday showed.

The Australian Institute of Company Directors/KPMG June quarter survey found business remains optimistic about the 12 month outlook for the domestic economy, with 64 percent of directors expecting a pick-up in economic conditions.

Over six months, 39 percent expected economic conditions to improve with the constuction/utilities sector the most optimistic and the wholesale/retail sector picking up from a pessimistic outlook last quarter.
The manufacturing and mining/agriculture sectors reported the weakest expectations for an economic improvement over the next six months.
The report said transport/communications and construction/utilities continued to report strong outlooks, the latter reflecting the recovery in housing and construction.

Asked about their own company's prospects compared with the same quarter last year, 54 percent of the 615 directors who responded said they were "more optimistic" against 52 percent in the March quarter survey.
By industry, this reflected an improvement in sentiment in the construction/utilities and retail/wholesale sectors, while manufacturing held last month's improvement.
KPMG executive chairman John Harkness said the results may reflect a sentiment that the worst is now behind these sectors.
Asked to compare expected profits in the June quarter against company budgets, "above budget" forecasts rose for the transport/communications and wholesale/retail sectors.
However, the outlook for the manufacturing sector deteriorated, with 45 percent of respondents reporting "below budget" expectations, against 33 percent in the previous survey.
Directors from the transport/communications sector and directors from the state of Victoria reported the strongest profit expectations for the September quarter.
